text:
You haven’t lived
until you have been in a
cheap boardinghouse
with nothing but one
bulb
and 56 men
crammed
in cots
and everyone
snoring at once
and some of those
snores
so
deep and
so crude and
incredible…
dark
guttural
inhuman
gasping
from hell itself.

It seems as if
your head were splitting
between those
sounds
of death.

And the
smells mingling:
dirty and
stiff socks and
underwear
with urine and
excrement
and above it all an air that
circulates slowly
very much like
that which comes from
uncovered garbage cans.

Those
bodies
in the darkness
fat
and thin
and hunched
some
without legs
without arms
others
without brains
and worst of
all: the total
absence of
hope
envelops them
covers them
completely.

It cannot be
borne.

You get up
go out
walk through
the streets
go up and down
sidewalks
pass buildings
turn the
corner
and go back up
the same street
thinking
all those men
were children
once
what
happened to them?

and what happened to
me?

it is dark
and cold
out
there.

translation.title: You Haven’t Lived...
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The sensory catalog, fragmented syntax, and line breaks are preserved.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
